769.t: Why he began opening on the cymbal; Zildjian and river cymbals
769.s: George wanted the cymbal for volume; he compares his 18-inch Zildjian with a river cymbal.
769.q: Yeah, because when I hit that fourth lick, it looked like the spirit just hit me to go right on then. Yeah. Because it starts right on the snap drum, just like George would tell me, he says, it sounds kind of dead. You understand? Yeah. It do sound dead starting off on the, on the, just on the…

871.t: Showing the drum set: lights, tuning and pearl snare
871.s: They look at the lights in his bass and snare drums, tuning pitch, the Ludwig snare and the sizzle cymbal.
871.q: Is there any particular note? That's OBC. Boy, that? Turn it up. Great. That's all your traps. Your big Chinese symbol is about 16 inches. Yeah. Yeah. I see this. That drum is almost. Boom. Yeah. We're going to have a hard zoom. We got a double card here for that. Yeah, we. Oh, here. Yeah, that she…

957.t: Snare drum make, Conn drums and tuning
957.s: He used Leedy and Conn drums, notes Conn made the first nickel-plated drums, and tuned snare to F and bass drum to D.
957.q: Yeah. Con's had drums in those days. Yeah. Say, the first one put out the nickel-plated drums.

865.t: Sizes of his bass drums and cymbals
865.s: He compares drum and cymbal sizes in the room and says a drummer needs good instruments.
865.q: Smaller than that. My gold drum back the bed is smaller than that. I think it's a, fourteen by eighteen. Yeah, this is a, a plenty smaller. Yeah, I guess it is. Yeah, when you get looking at it, yeah, it's, a little smaller you see. Oh yeah, it's, yeah, if that other's twenty-two then it's twenty,…

570.t: Bass drum with a light inside
570.s: Explains how a light bulb inside the bass drum keeps the head dry and tight in damp weather.
570.q: Well, no, it's easier to take down, take it down, and then it'd have a place for, you to set a light in it, you know? They had a place for them? Oh, yes, they got them in all bass drums mostly. Oh, they do? Mostly. Oh. On account of weather sometimes. If you catch a bass drum, it's a, anyway it…

829.t: Dance band drum kit and how he looks after and tunes his drums
829.s: Robertson describes his traps, stands and cymbals, how he keeps his drums wiped and ready, and loosens or tightens the heads with the weather.
829.q: What do you use? Yeah, all that in there. The whole... I got a tum tum nothing big. Big tum. Oh yeah, I got a tum tum big as that thing.

847.s: He prefers a 26-inch bass drum; smaller ones suit small combos in cocktail lounges.
847.ch: Drum sets, small bands and the depression
847.q: But those are really too small. Those are nice for combos, small combos playing in cabarets, you know, the cocktail lounge. But those 26 bass drums, what I like to play, I like to play. You got a lovely sound. You can hear it. I guess different drummers like different instruments playing. I like…

1041.s: On a later tape, Williams says he uses 21-inch Turkish cymbals and that drummers differ in their choices.
1041.q: Yeah, they're zinyin. The Turkish cymbals, that was run around 14, 22 or 21 inch too. Now that's what we use now. The regular good cymbals, most of the drummers, all the drummers don't use the same thing.

572.t: His drum kit, cowbells and the singer's name again
572.s: They discuss his Ludwig set and four cowbells, then return to the missing singer's name.
572.q: Tom's you had. You see, then, I mean, I fixed it out the way I wanted, and then, then later on, I finally, I, that's, that's a set of, that's a Ludwig set that I bought when I worked at Whirline, see.

943.s: Cymbals for big band versus small group, drummers bringing their own cymbals, and Joey Baron's different attitude.
943.q: Exactly. Yeah. Yeah there’s all sorts of things that, oh I mean you open a real can of worms — that’s why drummers have so many cymbals, unless they’re the leader of the band and can pick you know. But I mean the cymbals that you use for a big band probably you’re not going to use for a small…
